reason: Re-opened packet.js pali 6: Story VI.1 (A Poor Man Wins Spiritual Treasure) carries the evidence verbatim, the Teacher speaking of Radha after the Alinacitta Jataka: when a fault is pointed out a monk ought to be amenable to discipline like Radha and take no offence, and he who admonishes should be looked on as one who points out where treasures are to be found; it stands between the [106] and [107] markers, so Norman p. 106 holds (Book VI, vol. 2). Radha is Sariputta’s pupil in the story (your pupil). The Pali Tattha on 76 agrees (kopo na kātabbo, tuṭṭheneva bhavitabbaṃ, as the poor man shown treasure is glad). The paraphrase (take correction without offence like the pupil Radha; look on whoever admonishes as one pointing to treasure) matches the words without drift. Plain sense true to day.js: 76 opens chapter VI, The Wise Man, and speaks of whom to follow. verse.js ok (Dhammapada 76, at 75); entry-check ok, no warnings.
